paragraphs.source_en: The situation in the surrounding lands was growing ever more tense. Oda Nobuhide had appointed his son Nobuhiro lord of Anshō Castle and strengthened its defenses. Meanwhile, Lady Odai’s elder brother, Mizuno Nobumoto, bitterly resented her repudiation; his hostility was plain, and he watched Okazaki Castle like a tiger eyeing its prey. The Imagawa of Sunpu, for their part, had never abandoned their ambition of marching on the capital. Caught between these two mighty powers, the fate of the Matsudaira house looked darker even than the snow-laden sky that day.

paragraphs.source_en: Disputes that never arose in times of strength were certain to break out in times of weakness. It was bad enough that the clansmen were divided into pro-Oda and pro-Imagawa factions, but worse still was the danger that someone might see the weakness close at hand and conceive ambitions of his own. The Matsudaira clan would then splinter, bringing utter ruin upon the house. History, ancient and recent, offered no lack of such precedents. Hirotada’s great-uncle Matsudaira Nobusada had previously conspired with the Oda, and now his uncle, Kurando Nobutaka, had also begun repeatedly voicing discontent.
